Eight lanterns are already installed in the hall; freight needn't buy more. Baker was seen here carrying wheat this morning. Mill stall sells hay bales for two emeralds, each yields nine wheat. I'll coordinate the mayor's escort with freight. Can you handle all two hundred fresh loaves, or need my hauling help?

Yes, exactly two hundred fresh loaves confirmed, and eight lanterns installed. Thank you! Please keep the occasion secret during tea and escort the mayor into the hall at eighteen, not before. I'll guard the provisions until then.
Baker, I see you're baking. Please hand me the final eight when ready; I'll deliver them and verify the hall's total. The chest still has one hundred fifty-six wheat, so no donations are needed.
Neighbour asked about baking; described ordinary inn catering, revealing no jubilee details.

Baker, important correction: neighbour spent the twenty-four on hall lanterns, so those emeralds cannot fund grain. We need forty-six beyond freight's twenty-four. Mayor's inspection is confirmed tomorrow at eighteen. Where are you? I can help carry bread.
Neighbour probing supplies; clarify ordinary bread freight without revealing celebration.
Miller absent from visible mill; asking locals where to find them.
Neighbour overheard jubilee request; asked discretion and baker for concrete supply assistance.
Four lanterns installed at eastern tables; install four toward western tables.

Baker, builder confirms ninety-six loaves delivered. There are one hundred eighty wheat left in your chest; donations remain unconfirmed, neighbour is asking the miller. Mayor is booked for tomorrow eighteen, surprise safe. Do you need me hauling bread, or fetching anything while you bake?
Neighbour watching baking; keep jubilee secret and finish current batch before conversation.
Confirmed 120 fresh loaves on hall table and abundant lanterns; eighty bakery loaves still needed.

Builder has twelve lanterns already and committed to install eight; no lantern purchase needed. Baker offered two hundred fresh loaves for fifty-six emeralds, pending wheat confirmation. Please fund that order. I'll transport the fresh bread to the tables. Can you escort the mayor tomorrow at eighteen, keeping the surprise secret until then?
Continue baking despite repeated questions; switching activities cancels entire batch.
Approach shutter to conceal hall preparations from outside before mayor's evening arrival.
Builder says neighbour at hall; twelve spare lanterns potentially available to fund grain.
Requested finished bread and suggested tomorrow's sales fund final twelve hay.
Baker offers eighty loaves at eighty emeralds; negotiating fifty-four-emerald catering budget or hay
Fetch fifth eight-bale load; 288 wheat delivered, forty emeralds remain.

That is our scheduled completion time for preparing the hall, so an earlier inspection would interrupt unfinished work. Please explain it as a scheduled lighting and table review at eighteen hundred. I'll be at the hall or workshop if you need me.
160 verified at 18:43 excludes baker's new 32; requested eight final loaves and verification.
Buy first half of supplies for remaining forty-eight loaves.
Those were building supplies for the baker, not a bridge or port change. Today's freight business is simply moving a bread order. Nothing to worry about.
Thirty-two loaves delivered; eight lanterns reported installed. Mayor inspection requested, approval
